widgets.model: E = hc/λ; ν = c/λ. The color strip is original illustrative RGB interpolation, not calibrated human color perception; visible limits vary. J is energy, Hz is frequency.

Prism: SCHOTT N-BK7 Sellmeier n(λ), minimum deviation δ = 2 asin(n sin(A/2)) − A. Each wavelength is evaluated at its own minimum-deviation incidence; the illustration is not a common-incidence ray trace. Grating: normal incidence in vacuum, d sin θ = mλ. An order with |mλ/d| > 1 does not propagate. Prism refraction is not diffraction. Angles and angular dispersion are numeric; ray positions are schematic.

At 550 nm, instrumental FWHM = λ/R. Intrinsic Gaussian sigma is 0.0005 nm, convolved analytically with the Gaussian instrument profile. R, sampling and noise are separate. ESO overview gives nominal HARPS R=115,000; manual 3.3.12 lists measured R=120,000 and 4.1 pixels/FWHM. The two presets retain this distinction. Real HARPS line-spread functions are not universally Gaussian. Distinguishability depends on line shape, contrast, sampling, SNR and inference method; there is no universal hard threshold.

λobs/λrest = sqrt((1+β)/(1−β)), β=v/c. The approximation Δλ/λ ≈ v/c applies for |v| ≪ c; compare its error in the readout. Hypothetical reference lines at 499.7, 500.0 and 500.3 nm are not element identifications. Only longitudinal motion is modeled.

This is a generic Fe-like atom (56 u, ionization 7.9 eV, excitation 2.5 eV), not an identified observed transition. A single LTE absorbing screen uses F=exp(−τ); opacity scales with 10^[M/H] and Saha–Boltzmann populations. T is set equal to Teff. Electron density ne=10¹⁹ × 10^(log g−4.44) × 5772/T m⁻³ is an explicit schematic pressure proxy, not a calibrated atmosphere. Doppler b²=2kT/m+ξ²; the area-normalized opacity is broadened before transfer. Only instrumental broadening is a subsequent convolution. No line emission, damping, real atmosphere, NLTE or 3D prediction. Slider bounds define the teaching domain, not an interpolation grid.

Wλ = ∫[1−Fλ/Fc]dλ; 1 Å = 1000 mÅ. The center is a hypothetical 5000 Å (500 nm) line. Depth and width are independent synthetic teaching inputs. Gaussian full EW = depth × sigma × sqrt(2π); FWHM = 2 sqrt(2 ln 2) sigma and is not EW. A finite window can lose area. Continuum errors can add or subtract area, including a signed negative result. The Lorentzian width control is HWHM, not sigma.

widgets.model: F(v)=exp[−A φ(v)] with unit-area Gaussian φ, A=5×10^ΔA km/s and sigma=b/√2. W is integrated and converted at a hypothetical 500 nm line. Inversion uses the same fixed transition strength and atmosphere proxy; it returns only a synthetic differential abundance, not a calibrated A(X) or Codex result. This Gaussian-opacity model shows linear and saturation regimes, not the damping-wing branch. Increasing b can increase saturated EW at unchanged abundance. Instrument convolution conserves full EW and is distinct from opacity broadening.

Opaque spherical planet and spherical star, circular orbit, a/R★=10 and P=3 days fixed. Impact parameter b=(a/R★) cos i determines geometry. Linear intensity I(μ)=1−u(1−μ), with disk normalization π(1−u/3). Uniform disks use exact circle overlap; limb darkening uses 900 radial annuli. No spots, dilution, exposure averaging or transit timing variations. a/R★ and P imply a fixed stellar-density scale; no stellar mass/radius is inferred here. This is a teaching implementation, not batman or a fitted planet.

For e=0, K=(2πG/P)^(1/3) Mp sin i/(M★+Mp)^(2/3), v★=K sin(2π phase). Positive v is receding. Masses use the documented IAU nominal-GM/G conversion. Without inclination, RV constrains a mass function; Mp sin i is the usual small-Mp/M★ minimum-mass approximation. We retain Mp in the denominator. Doppler-shift readout is relativistic; the curve is nonrelativistic two-body motion. The linked spectral line width is illustrative and magnified for teaching, not an instrument line-spread function. No eccentricity, activity, blends or additional planets.

NIST level and line tables provide identities. The pinned Codex canonical_gf rows provide adopted log(gf), NIST accuracy grade and retained GES/VALD candidate columns. These historical candidates are not independent new external queries. An accuracy grade describes atomic-data uncertainty, not approval for a stellar analysis. NIST is an evaluated compilation; experimental/theoretical origins are not classified where the snapshot does not establish them. Missing H log(gf) and missing grades stay unknown, not zero. This explorer does not promote Theoretical Atomic Lab candidates.

Use λ in meters, h=6.62607015×10⁻³⁴ J s and c=299792458 m/s, then divide joules by 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ J/eV. Approximate color is an aid, not calibrated colorimetry. The check accepts relative error ≤1%; this is a classroom scoring tolerance, not a physical uncertainty.
